newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche to inform staff of branch revamp.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche to inform staff of branch revamp.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG said it would inform employee representatives on Wednesday about planned changes to its domestic branch network.

"We had a management board meeting on Tuesday and further bodies will be informed today, including employee representatives," a spokesman for Germany's largest bank said in response to a Reuter enquiry.
The spokesman declined to comment on a newspaper report that Deutsche planned to reduce the number of its main branches to eight or nine from 18.
Boersen-Zeitung on Wednesday reported that Deutsche planned to gain synergy benefits by merging functions like administration and transaction settlement.

Deutsche's 18 main branches act as regional headquarters, overseeing the bank's business in their respective areas. Two of the branches are in fact subsidiaries, Deutsche Bank Saar and Deutsche Bank Luebeck.

The main branches are responsible for legal affairs, accounting and settlement in their regions and have the same divisional organisation as the Frankfurt headquarters, with departments covering areas like retail customers, corporate clients and resources and controlling.
At present the network of main branches broadly corresponds with Germany's 16 federal states although North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany's most populous state, has several main branches.
Deutsche, like most major German banks, is trying to make its domestic branch network more profitable and already announced in May that it planned a regional reorganisation.
The bank is streamlining its entire branch network and has continued to reduce the number of its branches this year.
It had total of 1,652 branches in Germany at the end of September, down from 1,691 at the end of 1995. Its domestic workforce shrank by 2.6 percent or 1,336 people to 50,621.
The number of branches abroad fell to 782 from 803 but its staff abroad grew by 8.3 percent or 1,835 to 23,997.
